title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: Pushing the Limits of KV Cache Compression

main: §2.1–2.5 Architecture (overview, multimodal, CED, CSA2 modes, hierarchical sparse indexer, Single-Pass mHC, Engram, DSpark, FP4 main KV, optimization)
§3.1–3.2 Infrastructure (CSA2 training, Engram, persistent KV cache, SWA Bounded Replay)
§5.1–5.3 Post-training (task synthesis, RL, async infrastructure, OPD, Tables 3–4, Figures 9–10)
appendices: B scaffold and reasoning-effort details skimmed
reading_coverage.references: used for provenance (YOCO, IndexCache, Kimi-K3, GLM-5)
reading_coverage.method: downloaded official PDF v1; extracted full text with PyMuPDF; rendered pages 1 and 5 to read Figure 1(b) byte values and Figure 2 curves

supplementary_official_sources.used_for: compress_ratios (2 SWA, 18 encoder m=2, 20 decoder m=1), kv_source_layer_ids [2,8,14,20], index_source_layer_ids, candidate 2048 blocks x 8, engram_layer_ids [1,14]; no num_hash_layers field
V4.1 FP4 entry 288 B (256 B e2m1 + 32 E4M3 scales per 16 values); V4.1 FP8 entry 528 B; Q-norm only used in V4, not V4.1

claims.claim: 552B backbone + 196B Engram; 8B activated in prefill, 16B in decode; up to 1M context; 45T multimodal tokens
Global KV 890 bytes/token (always in HBM), ~1/4 of V4-Flash; persistent KV ~1/8 of V4-Flash; Figure 1(b): V1 389,120, V3.2 48,068, V4-Flash 3,514, V4.1-Flash 890 bytes
20-layer causal encoder + 20-layer decoder; decoder global KV projected from layer L/2 hidden states; prefill complexity O(NL) -> O(NL/2 + n_win L/2); inspired by YOCO

Full / Reindex / Reuse modes; each layer keeps own query and SWA KV; CSA2 removes overlapping compression and absolute positional embedding; indexer K projected from main KV; pure CSA2 replaces CSA–HCA hybrid

Layers 1–2 SWA; 18 encoder layers m=2 in 3 groups of 6 (Full + 5 Reuse); 20 decoder layers m=1 in 5 groups of 4 (first group Full, others Reindex, rest Reuse); 32 indexer heads, top-k 512; 64 query heads, head dim 512; 1 shared + 384 routed experts top-6, expert dim 2304; SwiGLU clamp 10
First decoder Full layer selects 2,048 blocks x 8 positions = 16,384 candidates; Reindex layers score only candidates; introduced in post-training, training-aware

E2M1 with one E4M3 scale per 16 channels (NVFP4 without global scale); max 448x6=2688 vs norm bound sqrt(512)~22.6, observed ~10; QAT in post-training; quantize after RoPE; SWA KV kept FP8; nearly halves storage vs V4 FP8 main KV; 'marginal' degradation

Exact SWA reconstruction needs L x n_win tokens; bounded replay uses last n_win tokens with truncated window; approximate, outputs depend on cache-hit position; 'negligible' / 'barely compromises' quality; decoder replay simulated in post-training

In V4 deployment SWA KV accounted for nearly half of persistent KV cache; V4's Zero SWA Caching exact recovery proved prohibitive in production; V4.1 moves SWA KV to 10% host-DRAM pool with minute TTL, global KV kept >=72h
Context 4K -> 1M increases single-token decode FLOPs by only 1/4; FLOPs weighted BF16/FP8/FP4 as 1/0.5/0.25

Single-Pass mHC traffic (4n+4)d -> (2n+2)d with negligible degradation; Engram 2 modules at layers 1 and 14, N-gram {2,3,4}, 8 heads, ~16M entries per head, FP8, short conv removed; DSpark 3 blocks, 5 draft positions, trained after pretraining with frozen backbone; MTP omitted in backbone pretraining
Head-wise Muon for Q and K (validated in GLM 5 and Kimi-K3); momentum + Sinkhorn balancing for embeddings, prediction head and Engram tables; Engram LR x5
Sparse attention trained from scratch at 64K without dense warmup; 1M at 34T tokens; batch 100.6M tokens; no instability; text:multimodal 7:1
V4-Flash / V4-Pro / V4.1-Flash base: MMLU-Pro 68.3/73.5/74.1; SimpleQA 30.1/55.2/42.3; LongBench-V2 44.7/51.5/45.2; MGSM 85.7/84.4/80.2
DeepSWE 74.2 (V4-Flash 54.4); Terminal-Bench 2.1 90.6 (82.7); Terminal-Bench 4.0 31.2 vs Opus-5 51.8; ExploitGym 15.3 vs GPT-5.6 Sol 33.7; scaffold spread DeepSWE 65.5–74.2; no MRCR/CorpusQA reported
No post-training algorithmic innovation; gains attributed essentially to data/environment pipelines; final OPD with over 40 teachers

Robustness boundaries not fully characterized; CSA2 selection errors and approximate SWA reconstruction may degrade capability in untested boundary cases; gap to frontier closed models on hardest tasks
890 = 2.5 entries/token x (288 FP4 main KV + 68 MXFP4 indexer key); V4-Flash 3,514 = 21 x (584+68)/4 + 20 x 584/128
claims.locator: derived from FlashMLA layouts and HF configs; indexer-key bytes are an assumption

boundaries: Compression costs (FP4 KV, bounded replay, CED, CSA2 reuse) are reported only qualitatively; no ablation numbers
No measured latency, TTFT or throughput; decode FLOPs are estimates
Base comparisons change data, scale, modality and Engram simultaneously
Training compute and hardware not disclosed
